# Introduction

We describe BMI–hypercapnia relationships within a selected acute-care cohort while exposing how historical source-entry pathways shape the observed population. These pathways record representation in reason-for-suspicion (RFS) source files; they do not necessarily identify every clinical criterion present at an encounter. Separating entry routes can change the observed association itself and does not eliminate outcome-dependent selection.

# Methods

## Source, eligibility and fixed index

The authenticated original FULL_DATA encounter list defines candidate visits. Adults had a 2022 emergency or inpatient encounter and available valid BMI ≥30 kg/m². Age uses the inherited birth-year proxy. Each patient contributes the first qualifying encounter before gas availability and adjustment completeness. Earlier unresolved eligibility, conflicting evidence and earliest-date ties remain unresolved. Later encounters never replace an obesity-only index.

BMI follows the approved encounter/prior reported-value hierarchy, followed by calculation from observed height and weight, with inherited rounding and validity rules. One-unit diagnostic bins around BMI 40 and 50 describe measurement and selection; they are not a regression-discontinuity design. No statistical BMI imputation is performed. Available BMI is not necessarily contemporaneous with the outcome. The audit reports measurement methods, lags, unknown chronology and consequences of the existing rules. Signed lags equal encounter-start date minus measurement date: positive means prior, zero means the same calendar day, and negative means later during the encounter. Component gaps are absolute differences between height and weight dates.

## Historical source-entry populations

A confirmed positive ABG, VBG, RESPFAIL, VENTSUPPORT or PREDISPOSITION source flag establishes the primary population, including encounters also represented through OBESITY. The principal selection sensitivity requires OBESITY membership and authenticated zeros in all five other families. Unknown flags remain unknown. All-six-zero discrepancies remain visible and require source investigation. RFS metadata are applied after the common index is selected.

The combined indexed cohort is a reconciliation reference. Non-OBESITY-only, overlapping and unknown-OBESITY/confirmed-non-OBESITY subgroups are descriptive. BMI ≥40 remains a descriptive stratum and is not equated with obesity-route membership. An overlapping all-OBESITY supporting analysis is confined to the audit.

## Outcomes and adjustment

Arterial hypercapnia requires ordinary authenticated ABG PaCO~2~ ≥45 mm Hg. Combined gas accepts ABG PaCO~2~ ≥45 or VBG PvCO~2~ ≥50 mm Hg; both specimens are not required. No pH restriction is applied. Strict validity limits are 5<arterial<200 and 10<venous<250 mm Hg, with reviewed units. Available-evidence negatives do not establish that an unmeasured specimen is normal. Unusable or unavailable outcomes remain unknown.

The ICD composite comprises J96.02, J96.12, J96.22, J96.92 and E66.2, with captured absence negative only under complete diagnosis capture. E66.2 introduces obesity-related ascertainment. Index-calendar-day gas sensitivities use collection date equal to encounter-start date, retaining the index.

Adjustment retains linear age and the inherited sex, combined race/ethnicity and geographic-region coding. Completeness means nonmissing values for inherited analysis variables, including retained Unknown categories. The White reference category includes non-Hispanic or unknown ethnicity; inherited race-category precedence is unchanged. Raw race × ethnicity cross-tabs are shown only when authenticated.

## Models, probabilities and uncertainty

Primary and obesity-only models are fitted separately. Each group's adjustment-complete BMI distribution supplies type-7 spline quantiles .05/.35/.65/.95: two interior knots, two boundaries and three natural-spline basis columns. The basis remains fixed within group across outcomes, timing, matched analyses and predictions. Current-measurement sensitivities reuse their parent basis. Constant outcomes, duplicate knots, separation, rank and convergence failures remain explicit without estimator substitution.

Gas curves standardize over each model's outcome-evaluable population; ICD uses known capture within group. Observation curves describe usable-evidence availability within group. No physiological outcomes are projected to untested patients. Fixed BMI 45 versus 40 contrasts require training-range support. Local counts and marginal covariate coverage expose sparsity even inside the global BMI range; these checks do not establish joint covariate support.

Pointwise 95% intervals use full coefficient covariance and condition on the empirical reference and fixed spline basis. They omit uncertainty from selection, measurement error and unmeasured confounding. Apparent calibration is in-sample; fitted/observed mean agreement is not independent validation.

## Secondary scenario and supporting checks

The named secondary scenario subtracts exactly one BMI unit when observed BMI >30; BMI=30 is unchanged. There is no floor or reselection. Paired predictions hold index, RFS membership and other covariates fixed. Reported quantities are observed and shifted mean probabilities, their signed difference and PIF=1−p_shifted/p_observed. Signed original-BMI-band contributions and their full covariance reproduce the total difference and variance. Marginal curve-density integration is not used.

Same-sample linear-BMI checks and matched ICD/gas analyses remain registered. A limited current-measurement sensitivity uses the already-selected BMI when reported at the index or calculated from height and weight both authenticated to that encounter. Full-cohort MAR/MNAR projections and IPW are excluded. The report is rendered from saved aggregates without clinical reads or refitting.

## Cohort partition and selection mechanisms

```{r}
bmi_report_table(a$rfs_semantics,"Source-pathway/outcome relationship and evidence status",keys="requirement")
bmi_report_table(a$rfs_outcomes,"Outcome evaluability and positivity by entry subgroup",keys="subgroup")
figure("RFS-flow");figure("RFS-entry")
bmi_report_table(a$prior_run_reconciliation,"Keyed reconciliation and unresolved comparisons",keys="requirement")
```

Inspect the obesity-only event counts before interpreting its curves. An outcome constrained by entry criteria is not independent physiological evidence; constant outcomes and nonestimability do not establish no BMI association. Source membership is never recoded from current outcomes.

```{r}
#| results: asis
for(group in c("primary","obesity_only")) {
 cat("\n## Source-entry population: ",group,"\n\n",sep="")
 v<-bmi_group_view(a,group)
 bmi_report_table(v$population_registry[v$population_registry$population_id %in% c("Q","C","missing_adjustment","C_icd","C_abg_encounter","C_any_gas_encounter"),],"Population and evidence accounting",keys="population_id")
 profile<-v$variable_summary[v$variable_summary$variable_id %in% c("bmi","age_at_encounter","sex","race_ethnicity","location") & v$variable_summary$population_id %in% c("Q","C","C_abg_encounter","C_any_gas_encounter"),]
 bmi_grouped_report(profile,"Participant profiles",groups="variable_id")
 bmi_scientific_results(v,"outcomes")
 figure(paste0(group,"/F1-A"));figure(paste0(group,"/F1-detail"))
 bmi_report_table(v$fixed_bmi_contrasts[v$fixed_bmi_contrasts$model_id %in% primary,],"Supported BMI 45 versus 40 contrasts",keys="model_id")
 bmi_scientific_results(v,"curves")
 bmi_report_table(v$bmi_basis,"Saved group-specific numeric basis",keys="basis_id")
 for(id in primary) {
  bmi_report_table(v$model_registry[v$model_registry$model_id==id,],"Encounter-wide spline fit status",keys="model_id")
  bmi_report_table(bmi_coefficient_view(v,id),"Complete primary coefficients",keys="Term")
  bmi_report_table(v$model_fit_diagnostics[v$model_fit_diagnostics$model_id==id,],"Apparent fit diagnostics",keys="metric")
 }
 bmi_report_table(bmi_pif_view(v,primary),"Secondary observed-population BMI scenario",keys="Model")
 figure(paste0(group,"/F2"))
 bmi_report_table(v$prediction_support,"Curve-grid and transformed support diagnostics",keys="model_id")
 bmi_report_table(v$timing_audit,"Fixed-index timing transitions",keys="outcome_id")
 bmi_report_table(v$linear_spline_comparison,"Same-sample linear checks",keys="outcome_id")
 for(o in c("abg","any_gas")){figure(paste0(group,"/F5-timing-",o));figure(paste0(group,"/F5-matched-",o))}
}
```

# Discussion and example conclusion

The revised analysis estimates BMI relationships separately by historical source-entry mechanism while preserving the same clinical episode. Agreement between groups is not required: their BMI distributions, observed outcomes and entry mechanisms differ. Separate confidence intervals do not constitute a between-group test, and subgroup PIFs must not be averaged.

A defensible conclusion should describe the direction and shape actually supported by the revised primary curves, then explain whether the obesity-only sensitivity is estimable and informative. No claim of preventable disease or treatment benefit follows from the secondary scenario. Selection into the original files, selective gas measurement, BMI timing and measurement uncertainty, residual confounding and sparse tails remain limitations.

The accompanying audit retains full model output, reconciliation and supporting analyses. Source acceptance, numerical review, visual inspection and investigator scientific approval are distinct states.

